entries.notes: Occitan name attested from the early 14th century (début du XIVe siècle); derived from Occitan 'cous' or 'cos', meaning a stony place. Also rendered 'La Coux'.
Variant Occitan spelling of the same toponym, attested alongside 'Las Coutz'.
French form of the Occitan toponym, attested as a noble estate name from the early 14th century. Used for the cave after its rediscovery in 1940.

events.description: On 12 September 1940, Marcel Ravidat discovered the entrance to the Lascaux cave. The cave walls were found to be covered with Palaeolithic animal depictions.

entries.notes: The cave paintings are attributed to the Magdalenian culture, c. 17,000 BC. The 'to' closes the entry at the end of the Magdalenian period; the cave was not continuously occupied thereafter.
Magdalenian cave used for parietal art, dated to approximately 17,000 BC. Closed with 'to' as occupation ended after the Palaeolithic period.
Rediscovered in 1940; designated a heritage site. Closed to the public since 1963; no resident community. Classified as ruins/uninhabited archaeological site under modern stewardship.
